question: Why can task vectors from separately fine-tuned pretrained models be added or negated with limited interference, and can explicit neural-tangent-space fine-tuning make this model editing more reliable?

key_findings.claim: Ordinary CLIP fine-tuning is materially nonlinear, so task arithmetic cannot be explained solely by post-hoc application of its NTK component.
key_findings.evidence: Across ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16, and ViT-L/14, the post-hoc first-order Taylor models have substantially lower single-task and absolute task-addition accuracy than the nonlinear fine-tuned networks. For eight-task addition, post-hoc linearization scores 57.1, 65.0, and 75.2 versus 71.4, 75.5, and 85.1 for nonlinear fine-tuning.

anchors.section: 3 Task arithmetic is not a consequence of linear fine-tuning

key_findings.claim: Training each task vector directly in the pretrained model's tangent space improves both eight-task addition and task negation over standard nonlinear task vectors.
key_findings.evidence: Linearized fine-tuning raises average absolute task-addition accuracy from 71.4 to 76.5 on ViT-B/32, 75.5 to 81.3 on ViT-B/16, and 85.1 to 88.5 on ViT-L/14. At 95% retained ImageNet control performance, target-task accuracy after negation falls from 24.0 to 10.9, 19.2 to 11.3, and 18.0 to 7.9, respectively, where lower is better.

anchors.section: D.2 Detailed results on task addition

key_findings.claim: The paper's weight-disentanglement property is mathematically equivalent to its task-arithmetic property and therefore names the desired noninterference behavior more than it independently explains its cause.
key_findings.evidence: Property 3 decomposes the edited function into task-vector-controlled components that vanish off each task support; Equation 5 then shows this is equivalent to Property 1, which already says each task vector changes outputs only on its own support. Disentanglement-error heatmaps operationalize violations and are useful diagnostics, but equivalence alone cannot establish a causal mechanism.

key_findings.claim: The finite-NTK spectra are consistent with cross-domain localization, but the aggregate local-energy plot does not by itself demonstrate individually localized eigenfunctions or necessity.
key_findings.evidence: The authors compute an SVD from only 200 training points per dataset and plot the sum of squared estimated functions, not individual supports. Proposition 2 gives localization only as a sufficient condition; the paper explicitly notes cancellation can yield task arithmetic without localized eigenfunctions, with necessity requiring local linear independence. Thus Figure 6 is suggestive evidence for low cross-domain coupling, not a unique spectral mechanism.

key_findings.claim: The random-initialization experiment does not isolate pretraining as the reason task arithmetic emerges.
key_findings.evidence: Random ViTs receive the same small-learning-rate, 2,000-step protocol chosen for pretrained fine-tuning, without a from-scratch hyperparameter search. Their average single-task accuracy is only 18.0-48.5% nonlinear, and multi-task arithmetic stays near 4.5-5.5%. This shows the tested random checkpoints do not merge, but training quality, optimization distance, data scale, and representation quality are all confounded with pretraining.

anchors.section: Table 3 and 6.2 Weight disentanglement emerges during pre-training
D.9 Further experiments with randomly-initialized networks

key_findings.claim: Linearization has substantial fixed-factor systems costs that matter when interpreting it as a practical editing method.
key_findings.evidence: The experiments use four 32GB V100 GPUs and under 350 GPU-hours. Appendix B states inference is usually two to three times slower, training-gradient computation roughly twice as costly, and training memory roughly doubled versus the nonlinear model. The main text's O(1) increase means asymptotic constant factor, not negligible overhead.

anchors.section: B Implementation aspects of linearized models

method.core_idea: Represent each downstream update as a task vector from a common pretrained checkpoint, diagnose cross-task interference in function space, and learn those vectors using the checkpoint's first-order Taylor model so their effects remain more separable.
method.mechanism: The study compares nonlinear fine-tuning, post-hoc Taylor expansion of nonlinear task vectors, and direct optimization of task vectors in a frozen finite-width NTK. It measures addition and negation, maps a two-vector disagreement surface over scaling coefficients, derives sufficient spectral localization conditions for noninterference, and compares pretrained with randomly initialized ViTs.
assumptions: Tasks have nonintersecting input supports, even though real semantic domains and label spaces may overlap.
All task-specific models share exactly the same pretrained parameterization and frozen CLIP classification construction.
Validation data are available to tune a shared task-vector scaling coefficient separately for every method.
Prediction disagreement is an adequate distance for diagnosing functional interaction.
A 200-point finite-NTK SVD and aggregate local energy reflect the relevant task-function basis.
The pretrained fine-tuning schedule is a fair control for training randomly initialized models.

techniques.role: Encodes a downstream adaptation as the difference between fine-tuned and pretrained weights.
Optimizes downstream updates directly in the checkpoint's first-order Taylor model.
Plots prediction interference over pairs of task-vector scale coefficients.
Uses finite-width kernel SVD and local energy to probe cross-domain functional support.
Tests whether comparable arithmetic appears without pretraining.

evaluations.setting: Eight CLIP vision tasks merged into ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16, and ViT-L/14 models.
evaluations.metric: Average absolute and single-task-normalized accuracy after task addition
evaluations.result: Tangent tuning reaches 76.5/85.4, 81.3/86.0, and 88.5/93.5, improving absolute accuracy by 3.4-5.8 points over nonlinear task arithmetic.
evaluations.baseline: Nonlinear fine-tuning, post-hoc linearization, and the pretrained checkpoint.

evaluations.setting: Eight task-negation cases with ImageNet as control and at least 95% of pretrained control accuracy retained.
evaluations.result: Tangent tuning achieves 10.9, 11.3, and 7.9, versus 24.0, 19.2, and 18.0 for nonlinear task vectors.
evaluations.baseline: Nonlinear task negation and post-hoc linearized negation.

evaluations.setting: ConvNeXt/CLIP, supervised ImageNet ViT-B/16, T5-Base on IMDB plus QASC, and random ViTs.
evaluations.result: The qualitative effect extends to a CNN and T5; linearized ConvNeXt improves 79.1 to 81.1, while the supervised closed-vocabulary model gains normalized but loses absolute accuracy and random ViTs fail to merge.
evaluations.baseline: Nonlinear variants for each architecture and random initialization.

limitations: Reviewer inference: the core eight-task benchmark uses small image classifiers sharing CLIP pretraining and does not establish behavior for modern instruction-tuned LLMs, heterogeneous objectives, or independently trained base models.
Reviewer inference: validation-set coefficient tuning remains necessary, so editing is not fully data-free and each baseline gets a separately optimized coefficient.
Reviewer inference: direct tangent training roughly doubles memory and training work and slows inference by two to three times.
Reviewer inference: weight disentanglement is defined as an equivalent restatement of successful task arithmetic, limiting its independent explanatory force.
Reviewer inference: aggregate finite-sample local energy is insufficient to identify localized eigenfunctions uniquely.
Reviewer inference: the random-initialization control is severely under-matched in accuracy and optimization, weakening the causal claim about pretraining.
Reviewer inference: task supports are assumed disjoint; overlapping domains, related labels, and conflicting tasks are exactly where merging is hardest.
failure_modes: Task vectors interact strongly once scale coefficients leave the small neighborhood in which the heatmaps are light.
A linearized model can be well disentangled yet have poor single-task accuracy, so normalized gains can hide absolute regression.
Shared or contradictory examples violate the disjoint-support abstraction and can require the same weights to implement incompatible outputs.
Coefficient selection can overfit the held-out training subset and fail under task mixture or distribution shift.
NTK linearization at one checkpoint cannot capture useful feature learning far from that checkpoint.
Random or weakly pretrained representations may have neither useful single-task functions nor mergeable update directions.
reusable_insights: Measure model merging as functional interference over scale coefficients, not only one final aggregate accuracy.
Separate single-task quality from merge retention; a method can improve one while harming the other.
Constrain updates to modules or subspaces whose function changes remain local, but test that locality on unseen mixtures and overlaps.
Use training-matched controls before attributing mergeability specifically to pretraining.
Spectral localization claims should display individual modes, truncation rules, robustness to sample size, and alternatives such as simple cross-domain kernel similarity.
open_questions: Can nonlinear fine-tuning be regularized for functional locality without paying the full tangent-model cost?
What pretraining objectives, data mixtures, or architectural features cause task-vector effects to localize?
How does the method behave when task supports overlap or labels conflict on the same inputs?
Can scale coefficients be selected without task validation data and remain reliable under changing task proportions?
Do tangent-space gains persist for large language models, LoRA adapters, and merges across independently trained or permuted checkpoints?
Which intervention establishes that the measured NTK localization, rather than another property of pretrained features, causes mergeability?

competitive_landscape.title: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic
competitive_landscape.difference: Ilharco et al. introduce task vectors, addition, negation, and analogies across vision and language. The present work supplies a functional noninterference definition and replaces ordinary updates with tangent-space-trained vectors.

competitive_landscape.title: TIES-Merging: Resolving Interference When Merging Models
competitive_landscape.difference: TIES trims small updates, resolves sign conflicts, and merges aligned parameters without tangent-model training. It attacks interference directly in weight space and is much cheaper at merge time, whereas this paper targets functional locality during fine-tuning.

competitive_landscape.title: Localizing Task Information for Improved Model Merging and Compression
competitive_landscape.difference: TALL-masks finds sparse, mostly nonoverlapping task supports in existing task vectors and Consensus Merging removes catastrophic weights, recovering over 99% of single-task accuracy in its reported settings without linearized inference. It operationalizes locality at parameter level and scales evaluation to 20 tasks.

competitive_landscape.title: Fine-Tuning Attention Modules Only: Enhancing Weight Disentanglement in Task Arithmetic
competitive_landscape.difference: Jin et al. explicitly target this method's doubled costs and reduced individual-model performance by fine-tuning only attention modules, arguing those modules exhibit sufficiently kernel-like behavior. It is a more deployable partial restriction but a narrower architectural prescription.

competitive_landscape.title: Multi-Task Model Merging via Adaptive Weight Disentanglement
competitive_landscape.difference: Adaptive Weight Disentanglement subtracts learned redundant components so task vectors become more orthogonal while preserving task performance. It treats interference as vector geometry rather than NTK function localization and avoids linearized inference, although it introduces its own optimization and norm assumptions.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Weight disentanglement is the fundamental requirement for task arithmetic, is acquired through pretraining, and can be amplified by fine-tuning in the pretrained model's tangent space.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Direct tangent-space task vectors improve addition and negation across three CLIP ViTs, display lower interference across coefficient maps, and coincide with finite-NTK energy concentrated on source-domain points; random ViTs do not merge under the tested protocol.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The practical tangent-training comparison and its consistent gains were novel and useful in 2023. The explanatory language is stronger than the evidence: disentanglement is definitionally equivalent to success, spectral localization is only one sufficient account, and the pretraining control is not training-matched. Later sparse, partial-linearization, and interference-resolution methods directly compete on cost and scale.

reviewer_notes: Read all 28 extracted pages and visually inspected the headline tables, nonlinear-advantage plots, coefficient heatmaps, tangent-space diagram, spectral-localization plots, implementation listing, and architecture/random controls. Five direct primary arXiv or OpenReview competitors, including 2024-2025 follow-ups, were checked on 2026-08-23.
